source.title: ICSE 2026 Examination: Geography (H.C.G. Paper 2)
source.subject: geography
source.authorityName: Council for the Indian School Certificate Examinations (CISCE)
source.notes: No official marking scheme is published with this paper; questions carry no official answer. ICSE 2026 board examination paper; paper code 'T26 502' printed on every page; session 'Main examination' taken from the official bundle name (ICSE-2026-MAIN). 14 printed pages plus 1 outline map of India (PDF page 15). Part I (30 marks, compulsory): Question 1 (five 2-mark sub-questions) is topographical map work on the supplied Survey of India Map Sheet No. G43S7, which is not in the PDF, so every Question 1 item is hasFigure true and confidence LOW; Question 2 (ten 1-mark items) is marking on the outline map of India, also hasFigure true and LOW; Question 3 is ten MCQs under a single printed [10], so 1 mark each is from the section instructions. Part II (50 marks): 'Attempt any five questions from this Part' over nine 10-mark questions (4-12); this is a pick-5-of-9 choice, not an OR pair, so choiceGroup is not used and the pack's marks total (120) exceeds maxMarks (80) by design. Marks are printed only per numbered sub-part, not per lettered item, so each numbered sub-part is kept as one entry with its lettered items (a)/(b)/(c) in the text rather than guessing a split. No cognitive-level tags are printed. Question 3 (vi)-(ix) on page 5 were checked in raw mode because layout mode separated the item numbers from their text. Five items depend on pictures or maps not reproduced (3(x), 4(ii), 5(i), 6(iii), 12(ii)) and are LOW.
source.usage: Official CISCE board examination paper from the CISCE Archive Library (cisce.org/archive-library); question text reproduced for study with attribution and a link to the original. Figures are not reproduced.

questions.text:

questions.text:
Shyam attended winter trekking camps in both Nainital and in Ooty. He observed that the mountains in Nainital were ice-covered, whereas, in Ooty they were ice-free.
(a) As a student of Geography, explain the reason for the difference in climate of Nainital and Ooty?
(b) If Shyam goes to Kochi in the same season, what difference of climate will he experience?

Study the climate data of station X and answer the following questions:
Month: Jan Feb Mar Apr May June July Aug Sep Oct Nov Dec
Temperature (ºC): 13.5 16.8 22.4 33.6 38.6 30.2 29.3 28.4 27.8 25.7 19.9 15.5
Rainfall (cm): 1.3 _ _ 5.9 12.4 43.9 51.4 39.8 20.9 15.1 2.6 2.1
(a) Why is there a decrease in temperature in the month of June after the high temperature of May?
(b) Calculate the total rainfall of the station during the rainy season and give your answer in cm.
(c) Is station X located near the sea or away from the sea? Give a reason for your answer.
extractionIssues: Climate data table on page 8 rebuilt as text rows from the PDF layout (12 values per row, in month order); the blanks ('_') for Feb and Mar rainfall are as printed. Check the column alignment against the PDF.

questions.text:
(a) Name the soil component derived from the decay of dead plants and animals.
(b) Why is the component mentioned by you in (a) important for agriculture?

Give a geographical reason to explain each of the following:
(a) In arid regions, trees are planted in rows perpendicular to wind direction.
(b) Black soil does not get leached.
(c) It is difficult to grow rice in red soil without the help of irrigation.

(a) What is soil conservation?
(b) Name two areas in north India where soil conservation is required.
(c) Name two methods of soil conservation practised in India.
Why are forests important for the Indian economy?

Identify the forest conservation methods described below:
(a) A sustainable system of managing a piece of land through combined production of agricultural crops, forest crops and animal rearing.
(b) Planting of trees along the side of roads, railway lines and on hill slopes.

Given below is an image of the forest found in marshy areas. Refer to the image and answer the questions that follow:
(a) Name the type of vegetation seen in the above image.
(b) Mention one adaptive feature of the trees of this vegetation.
(c) Name a region where this type of vegetation is commonly found in India.

questions.text:
Give one geographical reason to explain each of the following:
(a) Desert vegetation has long roots.
(b) At higher altitudes, trees are often conical in shape.
(c) Tropical Monsoon Forests are also called ‘Tropical Deciduous Forests’.

Raghu wants to irrigate his large field in a manner that will ensure uniform water distribution across the field along with water conservation.
(a) Name the irrigation method that will be suitable as per his need.
(b) How will the method of irrigation mentioned by you in (a) above help to conserve water?
What is the difference between Inundation canals and Perennial canals?

Considering the rapid depletion of groundwater and its implications for food and water security in India, sustainable management of groundwater resources is needed.
Source: [Journal of Hydrology, Volume 596, May 2021]
(a) How is ‘groundwater’ different from ‘surface water’?
(b) Why is the groundwater level rapidly declining in India?
(c) Name one conservation measure that will help in recharging of the groundwater.

Give a reason for each of the following:
(a) Wells are a common means of irrigation in Northern India.
(b) Many state governments have restricted the use of tubewells.
(c) Tank irrigation is a popular method of irrigation used in Karnataka.
State two advantages that Natural gas has over Coal.

(a) Umesh and Sagar are employed in iron ore mines in two different districts of Odisha. What are their possible places of work?
(b) State any two uses of copper.

(a) The Bhakra Nangal project is a joint venture of which state governments?
(b) Name the river on which this project is based.
(c) Mention two benefits of the Bhakra Nangal project.

Give one word for each of the following:
(a) The renewable energy produced by the natural rise and fall of ocean waters.
(b) An ore of aluminium.
(c) A mineral that is used to make steel strong and resistant to rusting.
Differentiate between subsistence farming and commercial farming.

(a) Name a state that leads in the production of jute.
(b) Mention a geographical factor that is responsible for the state mentioned in (a) above being the leading producer of jute.

(a) Why are Silver Oak trees and Cardamom trees planted in coffee plantations along with the coffee plants?
(b) State two climatic conditions that favour the cultivation of coffee.

(a) Name the cropping season in which Bajra is grown.
(b) Why is wheat not cultivated extensively in West Bengal and the extreme southern states of India?
(c) Why is the cultivation of soyabean gaining popularity in recent times?

‘Not all areas of India are suitable for establishing a large-scale industry.’
Give two reasons for the above statement.
‘The contribution of the electronics industry is crucial for the progress and development of the Indian economy.’ State two arguments in favour of this statement.

Give one geographical reason to explain each of the following:
(a) Work in sugar mills is a seasonal activity.
(b) The cotton textile industry is widely distributed in India.
(c) Vishakhapatnam steel plant has a unique locational advantage that enables it to procure raw materials easily and market the finished products with ease.

(a) Name the oldest iron and steel industry of India.
(b) Where is it located?
(c) Name a centre from where it gets its coal supply.
Inland water transport is more popular in Northern India as compared to Peninsular India. Give two reasons.
What is the purpose of developing the Golden Quadrilateral in India?

Mr. Kumar stays in Delhi with his family. Members of his family had to travel on Monday for different purposes. State the mode of transport that is most likely to be chosen by each:
(a) Mr. Kumar’s father wanted to travel comfortably to Patna to stay with his brother for a week.
(b) Mr. Kumar’s son had to attend a meeting in Ahmedabad that very evening.
(c) Mr. Kumar’s daughter had to meet her friend who lives in the same city, taking with her some fresh vegetables grown in their kitchen garden.

Give one geographical reason to explain each of the following:
(a) The presence of a number of ports has strengthened the transport sector of India.
(b) The number of airports in the country is on the rise.
(c) Railways are considered ideal for transportation of bulky goods over long distances.
What impact does waste accumulation have on our environment?

Study the picture given below and answer the questions that follow:
(a) Name the waste management practice shown in the given picture.
(b) State two benefits of this waste management practice.
